summary: Paged multi-row text/memo window: five body text rows, five 'next page' icons, five right-hand text rows and a numbered page indicator, plus a layout reference used to build the row animations.
evidence: Ui_PagedTextWindow_InitRows (0x0041DD7C) binds 'null_txt_l0' rows 0..4 through vtable+0x38, creates 'icon_next_0..4' at +0x4C..+0x5C, 'null_txt_r2_0..4' at +0x6C.. and page-number rows r4/r5; it is called by Ui_PagedTextWindow_InitRowsBase (0x0066D398) and Ui_PagedTextChildWindow_InitPanes (0x00403D88). The vtable 0x00782950 comes from the R2_006 score line. No base ctor is visible in the batch, so base is left empty.

summary: Two-page message window: a large message block at +0x54 and three 0x50-byte Ui_LayoutRef pages at +0x47C, +0x4CC and +0x51C that the destructor releases right-to-left.
evidence: Ui_DualMessageWindow_Delete (0x003A534C) calls Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self+0x51C), then at -0x50 (+0x4CC) and -0x50 (+0x47C). MessageWindow_Builder(self+0x54,...) plus FUN_00615058/FUN_0066BC6C operate on the +0x54 message block. Ui_DualMessageWindow_Update (0x003A4F58) drives the state bytes at +0x49..+0x4C.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ui_DualMessageWindow_Delete stores its vtable argument at *self before releasing the pages (ARM C++ deleting-dtor convention).

fields.name: maybe_pageState
fields.evidence: Update compares *(char*)(self+0x49) with 1 and 3 and writes 2: a small page/visibility state machine.

fields.name: maybe_pageActive
fields.evidence: Update: if (*(char*)(self+0x4A) == 0) { *(char*)(self+0x4A) = 1; } - a one-shot activation flag.

fields.name: maybe_flag4B
fields.evidence: Update writes 1 to +0x4B; no read is visible, so only the write pattern is known.

fields.name: maybe_flag4C
fields.evidence: Update writes 1 to +0x4C; no read is visible, so only the write pattern is known.

fields.name: messageWindow
fields.evidence: MessageWindow_Builder(self+0x54, 0x003A5094, ...) plus FUN_00615058/FUN_0066BC6C(self+0x54) build and query the message window embedded at +0x54 (first word only).

fields.name: pageLayoutA
fields.evidence: Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self+0x47C) is the last release in Ui_DualMessageWindow_Delete; one of the three 0x50-byte page layout refs.

fields.name: pageLayoutB
fields.evidence: Second release in the dtor chain: Ui_LayoutRef_Release(previous - 0x50) = +0x4CC.

fields.name: pageLayoutC
fields.evidence: First release in Ui_DualMessageWindow_Delete: Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self+0x51C).

summary: Window that wires five embedded child widgets: the widget bodies start at +0x80, +0x13C, +0x1F8, +0x2B4 and +0x31C, and pointers to them are kept at +0x384..+0x394.
evidence: Ui_FiveChildWindow_Init (0x00332F44; the dispatcher batch named the class Ui_FiveListWindow) stores self+0x80 at +0x384 (not one of this batch's offsets), self+0x13C at +0x388, self+0x1F8 at +0x38C, self+0x2B4 at +0x390 and self+0x31C at +0x394, then calls vtable+8 (attach owner) and vtable+0xC (reset) on each of the five children. No pane names identify the contents, so the child widgets are described positionally.

fields.name: childWidget0

fields.name: childWidget1

fields.name: childWidget2

fields.name: childWidget3

fields.name: childWidget4

summary: Four-slot icon row window: four slot-id bytes at +0x49..+0x4C, a refresh-enable flag and the standard Ui_Object-derived vtable.
evidence: Ui_FourRowIconWindow_Ctor (0x003F1D08) installs vtable 0x0076BAC4 and writes 0xFF over the four bytes +0x49..+0x4C. maybe_Ui_FourRowIconWindow_InitPanes (0x003F1AF0) rewrites them to 0xFF/1/0xFF/state or 0/1/2/3 depending on Ui_IsMode(3), and refreshes the four icon layers from the table at 0x007A9958.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ui_FourRowIconWindow_Ctor stores 0x0076BAC4 at *self; slot 0 is Ui_FourRowIconWindow_Dtor and slot 7 maybe_Ui_FourRowIconWindow_InitPanes.

fields.name: maybe_isRefreshEnabled

fields.name: slotId0
fields.evidence: The ctor writes 0xFF to +0x49; InitPanes sets it to 0xFF (mode 0) or 0 (mode 3). First of the four slot ids documented for the four-slot icon row.

fields.name: slotId1
fields.evidence: Set to 1 in both modes by InitPanes; second slot id.

fields.name: slotId2
fields.evidence: Set to 0xFF (mode 0) or 2 (mode 3) by InitPanes; third slot id.

fields.name: slotId3
fields.evidence: InitPanes stores uVar2 (0xFF or 3) at self->f_13 (= +0x4C); fourth slot id.

fields.evidence: Not an object field: only evidence is the virtual call (**(code**)(*param_1+0x34)) in InitPanes.

fields.name: unknown_offset_0xe0
fields.evidence: Not an object field: only evidence is the virtual call through slot +0x38 (null pane binding).

fields.name: unknown_offset_0x120
fields.evidence: Not an object field: only evidence is the virtual refresh call through slot +0x48.

summary: Item list/selection window: an embedded sub-object at +0x14, a u16 entry-id table and count at +0xE4/+0xEC, two float offsets, and an always-show flag.
evidence: Ui_ItemWindow_UpdateSelectionById (0x00421308) walks the u16 table at self[0x39] with a 4-u16 stride for self[0x3B] entries, calls Gfx_SpriteSetList_Select(self+6), writes 0x41E00000/0xC1900000 into self[0x3D]/self[0x3E] and copies them to the selected element at +0x64/+0x68. Ids 0x1E9/0x1EA/0x21B set the byte at +0x145 when the +0x144 gate is clear.

fields.name: maybe_subObject
fields.evidence: self[5] is dereferenced as an object and its vtable slot +0x14 is called: (**(code**)(self[5]+0x14))(self+5); an embedded helper object at +0x14.

fields.name: unknown_offset_0x50
fields.evidence: Not an object field: only evidence is the virtual call (**(code**)(*param_1+0x14))(param_1), which returns the selected element.

fields.name: entryIdTable
fields.evidence: puVar2 = (u16*)self[0x39] is walked with puVar3 += 4 (4 u16 = 8 bytes per entry) and compared with (itemId & 0xFFFF): the item-id table.

fields.name: entryCount
fields.evidence: The table end is puVar2 + self[0x3B]*4 (u16 units), so +0xEC is the number of 8-byte entries.

fields.name: maybe_offsetX
fields.evidence: self[0x3D] = 0x41E00000 (28.0f) and the same bits are copied to the selected element at +0x64; a horizontal position/offset.

fields.name: maybe_offsetY
fields.evidence: self[0x3E] = 0xC1900000 (-18.0f) and the same bits are copied to the selected element at +0x68; a vertical position/offset.

fields.name: maybe_isSelectionLocked
fields.evidence: UpdateSelectionById does nothing unless (char)self[0x51] (= +0x144) == 0, so this byte suppresses selection updates.

fields.name: isAlwaysShow
fields.evidence: Set to 1 for item ids 0x1E9/0x1EA/0x21B and to 0 otherwise; the flag is documented in the function doc as the always-show flag.

fields.name: unknown_offset_0x160
fields.evidence: Not an object field: only evidence is the virtual call through slot +0x58, iVar4=(**(code**)(*param_1+0x58))(param_1), whose result selects which offset pair is applied.
